like blossoms that bend to the breezes or showers,
Now wantonly winding, they flash, now they falter,
and, lingering, languish in radiant choir.

Eternal longings, Youth's inheritance,
All hopes that token immortality,
All griefs whereto immortal grief aspires.

sentences.text: All Nashville is a chill. And everywhere
Like desert sand, when the winds blow,
There is each moment sifted through the air,
A powdered blast of January snow.
You and I shall laugh together with the storm,
And together we shall dig graves for all that die in us,
And we shall stand in the sun with a will,
And we shall be dangerous.

Where evermore no green life shoots.

sentences.text: Look back with longing eyes and know that I will follow,
Lift me up in your love as a light wing lifts a swallow,
Let our flight be far in sun or windy rain—
But what if I heard my first love calling me again?
The sky is low, the clouds are mean,
A travelling flake of snow
Across a barn or through a rut
Debates if it will go.

sentences.text: Now silent, now singing and swaying and swinging,
like blossoms that bend to the breezes or showers,
Now wantonly winding, they flash, now they falter,
and, lingering, languish in radiant choir.
So mirrored in thy heart are all desires,
Eternal longings, Youth's inheritance,
All hopes that token immortality,
All griefs whereto immortal grief aspires.

There is each moment sifted through the air,

sentences.text: You and I shall laugh together with the storm,
And together we shall dig graves for all that die in us,
And we shall stand in the sun with a will,
And we shall be dangerous.

Like desert sand, when the winds blow,
There is each moment sifted through the air,
A powdered blast of January snow.

Was like the Stillness in the Air—
Between the Heaves of Storm—
The peasant whose lot was to sow and to reap,
The herdsman who climbed with his goats to the steep,
The beggar that wandered in search of his bread,
Have faded away like the grass that we tread.

In secret kept, in silence sealed;

Remember no man's foot can pass
Where evermore no green life shoots.

lessons.name: Select the misplaced or dangling modifier

header.text: <instructions>Select the misplaced or dangling modifier.</instructions>

contents.text: A modifier is a word or phrase that modifies, or describes, another word or phrase.

header.text: A misplaced modifier is a modifier that appears to modify the wrong word or phrase because it is too far from the word or phrase that it should modify.

sentences.text: Winston saw monkeys and peacocks on vacation in India.
This sentence has a misplaced modifier. It wrongly suggests that the monkeys and peacocks were on vacation.
On vacation in India, Winston saw monkeys and peacocks.
This sentence correctly suggests that Winston was on vacation.

header.text: A dangling modifier is a modifier that appears to modify the wrong word or phrase because the word or phrase that it should modify is missing from the sentence.

sentences.text: Trying to fall asleep, the sheets felt uncomfortably hot.
This sentence has a dangling modifier. It wrongly suggests that the sheets were trying to fall asleep.
Trying to fall asleep, I felt uncomfortably hot in the sheets.
This sentence correctly suggests that I was trying to fall asleep.

header.text: <instructions>Select the misplaced or dangling modifier.</instructions>
Sleeping in the hammock is a dangling modifier because it appears to modify the branches over Daniel's head. The sentence wrongly suggests that the branches were sleeping in the hammock.

This sentence has a misplaced modifier. It wrongly suggests that the monkeys and peacocks were on vacation.
On vacation in India, Winston saw monkeys and peacocks.
This sentence correctly suggests that Winston was on vacation.

header.text: A dangling modifier is a modifier that appears to modify the wrong word or phrase because the word or phrase that it should modify is missing from the sentence.

sentences.text: Trying to fall asleep, the sheets felt uncomfortably hot.
This sentence has a dangling modifier. It wrongly suggests that the sheets were trying to fall asleep.
Trying to fall asleep, I felt uncomfortably hot in the sheets.
This sentence correctly suggests that I was trying to fall asleep.
